pairs.why: Both put a few quiet sand rocks and a swirl backdrop around the palm, so staging and load are about equal.
B's backdrop is faint tone-on-tone icons on a wood floor, as in the real cards' quiet backdrops, while A's bold horseshoe pattern and grey ledge compete with the barrel.
Both float the hero on a quiet tone-on-tone ring field like the real cards, so staging gives no reason to choose.
Both use a flat sunburst field with the bottle floating, matching the real card's staging.
A hangs the clock on the stripes with a soft wall shadow like the real card, while B adds a floor ledge and ground shadow the real card doesn't have.
A's table is bigger and more central with slightly fewer small background shapes, while B pushes the table small into a busier bush and tree backdrop.
Both place the light under a truss on a soft blue field; the extra yellow rivets in B and the lighter truss in A roughly offset each other.
A's bold wavy backdrop and simpler pool edge are closer to the real card, while B's busier ripples, thin rails and softer waves are less like it.
